m.d: An apartment is a place with several rooms in a building where other people also live.
m.e: The woman moved her furniture into her new apartment.

m.d: If you appreciate something, you understand its value or its qualities
m.e: It's hard to appreciate how difficult the job is until you try it yourself.

m.d: If you appreciate something, you feel thankful for it.
m.e: Thanks so much for your help! I really appreciate the gift.

m.d: If something appreciates, its value increases.
If two things are apart, there is space between them.
m.e: Scientists theorize that Pangaea drifted apart into the different continents that exist on Earth today.

m.d: You use something apart to leave that thing out of the topic.
m.e: The lies apart, they're good workers.

m.d: An applause is to show praise or enjoyment of a music or play by hitting hands together many times with sounds (clapping).
m.e: Please give a round of applause to this wonderful band for their music!

m.d: You use apparently to indicate that the information you are giving is something that you have heard or seen, but you are not certain that it is true.
m.e: Oil prices fell this week to their lowest level in fourteen months, apparently because of over-production.

m.d: If you apologize, then you say you are sorry.
m.e: He apologized because he had accidentally bumped into someone.

m.d: If something appears a certain way, it looks or seems that way.
m.e: At first glance, this would appear to be true.

m.d: If something appears, it comes into sight.
m.e: She was studying when her mother appeared in the doorway.

m.d: If something appears in a book, movie, TV program, etc., it is in it.
m.e: He has appeared in over 100 movies.

m.d: An appointment is a formal agreement to meet or visit someone (for example, a doctor) at a certain time and place.
m.e: I have a doctor's appointment at 3:00 tomorrow.

m.d: April is the fourth (4th) month of the year.
m.e: There are 30 days in April.

m.d: April is a female given name.
An approach is a way of doing something.
m.e: We need children and adults to take a proactive approach to reducing gun violence.

m.d: An approach is movement towards something.
m.e: And he made a cautious approach to the boat.

m.d: An approach is the road or path that leads to a place.
m.e: There were cameras on all approaches to the house.

m.d: If you approach something, you move closer to it.
m.e: We're now approaching the last bus stop. Please move towards the door.

m.d: If you approach a problem, or a job you try to deal with it.
m.e: We've got a difficult situation here, and I'm not sure how to approach it.

m.d: An apple is a sweet, red, yellow or green fruit.
m.e: I gave my teacher an apple.

m.d: Big Apple is a name for New York City.
m.e: I went to the Big Apple.

m.d: An apology is words or actions that show you are sorry.
m.e: Thank you both very much, and again, my apologies for keeping you both waiting so late.

m.d: If you make no apologies for something, you think it was the right thing to do.
m.e: The company president makes no apologies for those high profits, saying people should be pleased the industry is so strong.

m.d: If a rule, a principle, a law, etc. applies, it has some effect on the situation.
m.e: The new anti-smoking law applies only to public buildings.

m.d: If you apply for something, you formally say that you want it or you want to do it.
m.e: After high school, he applied to three universities and was accepted by all of them.

m.d: If you apply something such as an idea, rule, formula, or piece of information, etc., you use it to do something, work with something, or handle a situation.
m.e: I found it hard to apply the principles I learned at school to the problems I faced at work.

m.d: An appeal is a strong or official request.
m.e: In an emotional appeal, Sevan asked the two groups to stop the fighting.

m.d: An appeal is a request for an earlier decision to be changed, especially in law.
m.e: Her application was refused, her appeal was rejected, and when she failed to leave, she was arrested.

m.d: If something has appeal, people have good feelings about it, like it, or want it.
m.e: It was a type of game that had universal appeal to male and female.

m.d: If you appeal for something, you ask for it, often strongly or officially.
m.e: The people appealed for help as huge fires advanced towards their homes.

m.d: If you appeal a decision, you ask for it to be changed, especially in law.
m.e: The defense notified the State Supreme Court that it would appeal the conviction.

m.d: If you something appeals to you, you have good feelings about it, like it, or want it.
m.e: Adventure, money, sex, and violence appeal to large numbers of people.

m.d: If you appropriate something, you take it from somebody else and make it your own.
m.e: By the end of this year, the total funds appropriated will be nearly $600 billion.

m.d: If something is appropriate, it matches the situation.
m.e: We suggest ways in which teachers may change their materials to make them more appropriate for bilingual students.

If a person in power approves something such as a plan, a sale, a rule, etc., they say it is OK and it may go ahead.
m.e: Voters there have approved a plan to remove most cars from the city center.

m.d: If you approve of something, you think it is good.
m.e: The latest survey shows that only 32 percent approve of the way the president is handling his job.

m.d: An application is a request for something. Often it is a paper form that you have to fill out to ask for something.
m.e: She filled out her applications for college and hoped she would hear soon whether she was accepted to any schools.

m.d: An application is the way something is used.
m.e: The application of the new laws made things much more fair in the country.

m.d: If something has an application, it can be used.
m.e: She liked studying Latin in college, but found that a degree in Latin had few applications in the real world.

m.d: When you have appetite, you feel hungry and would like to eat some food.
m.e: My blocked nose is making me lose appetite.

m.d: If you apologise, then you say you are sorry.
m.e: He apologised because he had accidentally bumped into someone.

m.d: Approval is when you formally allow something to happen.
m.e: The treaty requires approval by Parliament.

m.d: Approximately is close to, but not exactly.
m.e: Approximately $150 million is to be spent on improvements.

If something is apparent, it is easy to see, realise or understand.
m.e: When she was nine, for no apparent reason, she began to dislike the classes.

m.d: appearing or seeming to be a certain way.
m.e: The difference was more apparent than real.

m.d: An app is a computer application.

m.d: An appreciation of something is the ability to see it's value and understand it.

m.d: Appreciation is the feeling of being thankful.
m.e: I just wanted to send you this card to show my appreciation for your kindness last week.

m.d: Appreciation is the rise in value of something.
m.e: The appreciation of the Japanese yen against the US dollar has helped the American automobile industry.

m.d: If you appoint someone to a job or position, you give the job to them.
m.e: The president appointed her to investigate the problems.

m.d: If you appoint a time for something, you choose that time.

If someone is apt, they have a natural ability to do something or learn something easily.
m.e: She is an apt student who picks up new concepts quickly.

m.d: If something is apt, it is suitable or appropriate in the circumstances.
m.e: That comment was particularly apt given the situation.

m.d: When someone is likely to do something, they are described as being apt to do it.
m.e: He is apt to forget his keys if he's in a hurry.
